Draft a blog entry and get it approved **before** anything is published.

> **This implements CLAUDE.md Non-Negotiable Rule 13 — absolute, no exceptions.** Every language,
> every site, every length; translations, LSJ issues, community-authored and cron-drafted posts
> included. There is no post small enough to skip it, and approval of a different post is not
> approval of this one.

Usage: `/blog-draft <slug>` — or `/blog-draft <slug> "<what the post is about>"`.
Existing draft? Same command reopens it at whatever stage it is in.

Input: $ARGUMENTS

## Why this exists (do not shortcut it)

The HIC has asked repeatedly to review blog text as a copy-paste block before
publication, and it kept not happening — sessions published with nothing shown,
or drafted a post that was never published, or surfaced an audit summary instead
of the actual words. Every one of those was an agent treating "show the draft" as
something to remember.

So it is enforced. `.claude/hooks/blog-draft-gate.sh` blocks `Write`/`Edit` on any
file under `*/posts/*.html` unless `docs/blog-drafts/<slug>.md` exists **and**
contains a line reading exactly `Status: APPROVED`.

The hook cannot verify a human read anything. It only guarantees the text exists
in a readable form and that approving is a deliberate, diffable act. **The asking
is still your job.**

## The loop

### 1. Draft

Write the full post text to `docs/blog-drafts/<slug>.md`:

```
Status: DRAFT
Slug: <slug>
Title: <title>
Language: <fi|en|...>
Target: onelifetime.world/posts/<slug>.html
Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>

<the complete body text — every word that will appear on the page>
```

Plain prose. No HTML. This file is what the HIC reads, so it must be the whole
post, not a summary, outline or description of the post.

### 2. Show

Output the **entire draft in one fenced code block** — per the CLAUDE.md
Deliverable Handoff Rule, a fenced block is the only thing with a copy button.

- One block. Not several. Not a preamble the HIC has to scroll past.
- The whole text, however long. Truncating defeats the purpose.
- Then **stop and ask.** Do not publish in the same turn. Do not move on to the
  next task and leave the question hanging.

Ask one concrete question: approve as-is, or what to change.

### 3. Revise

Take edits at whatever grain the HIC gives them — a sentence, a section, the
whole angle. After each round, re-emit the **full** text in one block, not a
diff. They are reviewing the finished thing, not the change.

If the HIC prefers line-by-line confirmation, use the `/dialog` convention:
propose each change as `muutos;` *current sentence* → *improved sentence* and
apply on `agree`.

### 4. Approve

Only when the HIC says so explicitly, about **this** post, set:

```
Status: APPROVED
```

Never flip that line on their behalf, on a general "go ahead", or on approval
that was about something else. It is the record that they saw the text.

### 5. Publish

Now the gate opens. Build the HTML post, register it per
`docs/BLOG_STANDARD.md` §3 / §3.1 (post registry, `latestPosts`, injector),
sync the dual folder, and — if the post ships in more than one language —
follow §3.2 and §3.2.1, which include the mandatory AI-content label on any
machine-translated variant.

Then tell the HIC where it landed: the file path and the live URL.

## Failure modes this is meant to kill

| Symptom | What went wrong | The rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published, HIC never saw the text | Draft step skipped | The gate blocks it |
| Drafted, never published | Loop abandoned mid-way | A `Status: DRAFT` file is unfinished work — surface it, do not leave it |
| HIC saw an audit/summary, not the post | Showed *about* the text | Step 2 is the full text, in one block |
| HIC approved, wording changed after | Edited post-approval | Any post-approval edit reopens the loop |

## Open drafts

Anything in `docs/blog-drafts/` still marked `Status: DRAFT` is unpublished work
awaiting the HIC. List them when asked what is pending, and at session end.
